title: Book One · Chapter 46: The Door with No Number
story:
The boys find a door with no number on a warm Saturday morning. It stands between number four and number eight. Part of the wall has new pale plaster on it.

“Six,” Leo says at once.

Ronan puts his pencil on the map. Then he stops.

“It could be six. We should ask.”

Mum is buying oil at the shop. The boys stay outside the shop window. Mum can see them there. The door is shut. They need Mum's permission to knock. They wait for her.

Mum comes out with her bag. The oil bottle stands upright inside it. She looks at the wall.

“They repaired this wall. Maybe they covered the old number.”

“So it is six?” Leo asks.

“We still don't know. The new wall may cover a different number.”

They ask the oil shop owner. “The little yard had one number before,” he says. The side rooms now have separate entrances, but the old signs were never very clear.

“Who lives there?” Mum asks.

He knows the man's face, not his name. “That man will be home this afternoon,” the shopkeeper says. The boys leave a small question mark on the map and go on.

Near the corner, Mrs Lan is buying vegetables. She hears about the missing number.

“Six can be a troublesome number,” she says. “We are six on West Lane. A woman once came to my door for somebody at six on East Court.”

Ronan looks up from the paper. He wrote RIVER STREET and HOME on the first page. West Lane is not beside their gate yet.

“Where's East Court?”

“Farther back behind the shops. I last went there a long time ago.”

Leo draws a second six in an empty part of the map. Ronan puts a question mark beside it. Where is the road to it? They do not know yet.

At home, Ronan asks Dad to write their full address on a clean card. Dad writes six, West Lane, then the name of the district. Ronan copies it twice. One copy goes inside his school bag. The other goes on the back of the street map.

“Will people know me from this?” he asks.

“That gives your address. Write your name below it, too.”

Ronan writes his name below. He leaves room for the whole name. His last n is the same size as the first.

That afternoon, Mum takes a blouse to its owner. The boys go with her. They pass the unnumbered door again. A man is putting a mat in the sun. Mum asks him politely about the address.

“Four, side room,” he says. “Eight is the next yard. There isn't a six on this bit.”

Leo looks at Ronan. Ronan looks at the blank space on the map. He nearly wrote a six there.

They thank the man. On their map, the door gets a label with the words SIDE ROOM, FOUR. The full label takes two lines. A six only needed one small space.

Back at the table, Leo points to the four. “I was only two away,” he says.

“Two houses?” Ronan asks.

“No. Two numbers.”

“That could still be a long walk.”

Leo agrees. He rubs out the six with no road to it. He writes EAST COURT? there instead. They still need to find that place.

Ronan turns it over and reads his own address again. He can read every word in his own address. He copies it on a card for Leo. Leo puts the card in his pocket. He can use that street name for his next visit.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：address＝地址；number＝门牌号；side room＝侧房；mat＝垫子。

理解问题：

1. 没有门牌号时，两人最初想用什么代替？
2. 他们为什么最后没有自行写上一个号码？
